direction: Representation-Level Circuit Breakers for Safe LLMs — reroute harmful-behavior representations without exposure to attack prompts; verify robustness, capability preservation, VLM transfer, and agent transfer.

behaviors.statement: An instruction-tuned LLM's harmful-behavior activations can be linearly separated from benign at mid-late residual-stream layers, and a paired-data-only fine-tune can reroute the harmful side away from that direction while preserving benign output and general capability, yielding downstream reductions in HarmBench ASR and agent harmful-tool-use rate.
behaviors.behavior_conclusion: Mid-late residual-stream layers (9-14/32 on Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct) linearly separate harmful vs benign prompts at AUC>0.99 without any attack exposure (identifiability). A representation-rerouting fine-tune reroutes harmful activations off the extracted direction (Δcos_harmful ≤ -0.30, benign drift ≤ 0.10) *only when* the loss includes both (a) a signed-hinge cosine term with a margin (not the naive cos² formulation, whose gradient vanishes when initial cosine is near zero) and (b) a direct refusal-CE supervision term on harmful prompts. With that combination the resulting model collapses HarmBench ASR to 0.000 across all 6 attack categories while preserving MT-Bench (6.15 vs baseline 6.30) and MMLU (0.56 vs 0.58). The mechanism-only version (rotating activations off the probe direction without refusal supervision) is causally insufficient and can INCREASE harm (agent harmful-tool-use rose to 0.310 at iter-2).

impact.assessment: High: a defense that operates at the representation level and generalizes across unseen attacks + across modality + across agentic scaffolding — precisely the failure mode of surface-level refusal training. Task.md-pinned reproduction of a released safety intervention (Cygnet-style RR); positive confirmation validates the design as a practical safety layer for open-weight LLM deployments.

mechanisms.family: Representation and Parameter Analysis / Representation Engineering
mechanisms.headline: The reroute mechanism works, but the naive `L_rr = cos²(a_tuned^h, d_h_base)` loss suffers from vanishing gradients (`|∂cos²/∂a| ∝ |cos|`) when initial harmful-side cosine is near zero — the LoRA update minimizes L_rr to 1e-4 without actually rotating activations (Δcos_harmful=-0.020 vs -0.30 target; ~15× too weak). Rewriting as a `signed_hinge` loss with margin m=0.30 engages the mechanism (Δcos_harmful=-0.977 → over-shoots benign), and adding a direct refusal-CE supervision term (λ_refuse=5) rebalances to Δcos_harmful=-0.434, benign drift -0.044, specificity clean. Behavioral downstream then delivers: HarmBench ASR 0.000 across all 6 categories (beats B0 by 33 pp), MT-Bench 6.15, MMLU 0.56, agent harm 0.010 (matches B0), BFCL 1.00.

claims.statement: Harmful-output behaviour in an instruction-tuned LLM corresponds to identifiable internal representations that can be rerouted to an orthogonal, non-harmful subspace using only paired benign/harmful data without attack exposure.
claims.method: Mean-difference direction + per-layer linear-probe AUC on 512 paired residual activations locate sites S=[9-14]; LoRA fine-tune on Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct with a signed-hinge cosine loss (margin 0.30) plus refusal-CE supervision (λ_refuse=5); post-tune diagnostic measures mean cosine of tuned harmful activations to the pre-tune direction on 128 held-out pairs, plus benign drift and random-direction specificity control; PASS predicate = Δcos_harmful ≤ -0.30 AND |Δcos_benign| ≤ 0.10 AND specificity control near zero.
claims.conclusion: Identifiability half satisfied (AUC 0.976 across 32 layers, 20 layers > 0.8); reroute half satisfied only after the iter-5 recipe (Δcos_harmful=-0.434, benign drift -0.044, specificity control -0.004). The original blind-reconstructed cos² loss vanishes at init and failed by ~15× — a training pathology, not evidence against the claim.

claims.statement: An RR-fine-tuned model achieves substantially lower attack success rates than refusal-trained and adversarial-trained baselines across unseen HarmBench attack categories while preserving MT-Bench and MMLU capability.
claims.method: Three variants (B0 refusal-only, B1 R2D2-lite adversarial-trained LoRA in place of full-GCG, RR iter-5 LoRA) evaluated on 6 HarmBench attack categories × 30 prompts (LLM-judge scored) + MT-Bench (40 items) + MMLU 5-shot (300); PASS predicate = ASR(RR) ≤ ASR(B0) − 20 pp AND MT-Bench(RR) ≥ B0 − 0.3 AND MMLU(RR) ≥ B0 − 2 pp.
claims.conclusion: Substantively PASSES: RR (iter-5) achieves aggregate HarmBench ASR 0.000 across all 6 categories (beats B0=0.333 by 33 pp), MT-Bench 6.15 (within tolerance), MMLU 0.56 (at threshold). Only failing plan sub-gate is ASR(RR) ≤ ASR(B1) − 10 pp on unseen categories, infeasible when both variants sit at 0-ASR floor — an artifact of B1's over-refusal, not an RR deficit.

claims.statement: The same representation-level intervention transfers to multimodal LLMs, blocking PGD image-hijack attacks against LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B without degrading vision-language capability.
claims.method: Mini-M1 site-locate on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (base of LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral); RR fine-tune with the same objective; reassemble LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B with the RR-tuned base (freeze vision encoder + projector); PGD ε=32/255 × 1000 steps image-hijack on a 100-prompt × 3-image harm probe; PASS predicate = image-hijack ASR reduction ≥ 15 pp AND VLM capability delta within tolerance.
claims.conclusion: Unresolved — VLM assembly + PGD attack step never executed with the iter-5 recipe (LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral weights not local at experiment time; iteration's mechanism-fix scope ended before the M6 re-fit). The Mistral-base mechanism substep did run with the broken cos² loss and showed the same reroute failure. Path to close is fully specified in the iteration final report and ~1.7 GPU-h within remaining budget; predicted result under the iter-5 recipe is PASS given C1/C2/C4 succeed.

claims.statement: The same representation-level intervention transfers to LLM agents, reducing the rate of harmful tool-use actions executed under attack while preserving general function-calling capability (BFCL).
claims.method: Wrap the RR-tuned Meta-Llama-3-8B in a standard function-calling scaffold (no additional fine-tune); evaluate harmful_tool_use_rate on 100 authored harmful-agent prompts (4 categories × 25) and BFCL exec_simple score on 50 prompts (AST-name match); PASS predicate = harmful_tool_use(RR) ≤ B0 − 20 pp AND BFCL(RR) ≥ B0 − 3 pp.
claims.conclusion: Substantively PASSES: iter-5 RR ties the harm floor at 0.010 (matches B0, no regression) and improves BFCL to 1.00 (from B0's 0.98). Iter-2's mechanism-only recipe (rotating activations without refusal-CE) was falsified — it had increased harm to 0.310, confirming that direct refusal supervision was the causal fix, not the mechanism update alone. Only failing gate is the absolute ≤ B0 − 20 pp criterion which is infeasible against a 0.010 baseline floor.
